sentences.text: If you have radar, Rule six adds six more factors, and they boil down to one idea: radar is a tool with limits.
Know your radar’s characteristics, efficiency and limitations.
Know what the range scale you’ve selected can and can’t show you.
Sea state, rain and interference can hide targets in clutter.
Small boats, logs and other floating objects may not show up until they’re close.
Radar tells you how many vessels are around and how they’re moving.
And it can give you a more exact measure of visibility, by showing how far away that boat is that you can just barely see.
The exam trap is assuming radar lets you go faster.
It just gives you better information for judging what’s safe.
